subject: Human Evolution
title: Bone and Antler Tools
description: One-minute skill: Bone and Antler Tools.

hook.text: Stone gets the glory, but bone tools are just as ancient—and far more versatile.

buildup.text: Bone can be carved into needles, fishhooks, and harpoon points that stone can't replicate.

discovery.text: A 90,000-year-old bone point from Congo's Katanda site is ground smooth—clearly shaped by human hands.

twist.text: Bone rarely survives in the fossil record. Stone tools dominate simply because stone lasts forever.

climax.text: The 'Stone Age' label hides a rich organic toolkit that has mostly rotted away over millennia.

punchline.text: The Stone Age was never just about stone.

quiz.question: Why do we know less about bone tools than stone tools?
options: Bone decomposes, so fewer survive in the fossil record
